title: us house take up russia sanctions bill backed by late senator graham 2026 09 11
text:
WASHINGTON, Sept 11 (Reuters) - The U.S. House of Representatives will begin consideration next ​week of a sweeping Russia sanctions bill championed by the ‌late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, which has passed the Senate but faces stiff opposition from House Democrats.
The House Rules ​Committee said it scheduled a meeting to consider the ​measure for Monday afternoon. Approval by the Republican-majority ⁠Rules Committee would pave the way for a ​vote in the full chamber later in the week.
Graham, ​a South Carolina Republican who died in July, was among Ukraine's most outspoken allies in Congress. His bill aims to ​increase economic pressure on Moscow over its invasion ​of Ukraine by sanctioning Russian officials and authorizing stiff tariffs ‌on ⁠China, India and other countries to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas. The Senate voted 86-11 last month to pass the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia ​and Iran Act ​of 2026."
However, ⁠the support from both Republicans and Democrats that propelled the bill through the ​Senate might not be enough to ​secure ⁠House passage.
Some lawmakers and industries worry that new tariff powers for Republican President Donald Trump could raise costs ⁠for ​U.S. importers and consumers. Some ​Republican lawmakers are also concerned about political blowback ahead of November's ​mid-term elections.
